chapters.title: Chapter 2: The New Multipolar World: US, China, and the Rest

lessons.title: Case Study: Semiconductor Export Controls and Their Ripple Effect on Indian IT and Auto Stocks

body.text: No chip export control was ever aimed at India. Yet the fallout reached two of its largest sectors at once, hurting auto production through supply chains while quietly boosting India's role as the world's chip design back office.

children.text: Chapter 2 has covered tariffs, tech decoupling, supply chain realignment, and sanctions as separate ideas. This closing case study shows how they overlap in a single, ongoing story: the global semiconductor export control regime that began in October 2022, and its very different effects on two large Indian sectors, automobiles and information technology.
The Timeline: From Shortage to Structural Shift

body.title: Chips, Shortage, Controls, and India's Response

events.title: The global chip shortage
events.description: COVID-era demand swings, factory shutdowns, and a scramble for consumer electronics chips left auto manufacturers worldwide, including in India, unable to source enough semiconductors, causing production cuts and long waiting periods for new vehicles.

events.title: US export controls begin
events.description: The controls covered in the previous lesson restricted advanced chip and chipmaking equipment exports to China, layering a new, structural geopolitical constraint on top of the shortage's cyclical supply-demand problem.

events.title: Controls widen, India's own plants break ground
events.description: As controls tightened further and allies aligned their own export rules, India's own semiconductor push accelerated, including Micron's chip assembly and testing plant in Sanand, Gujarat, and Tata Electronics' semiconductor assembly facility, both aimed partly at reducing this exact dependency over time.

body.text: Keep these two ideas separate, because this case study involves both. The 2021 chip shortage was a cyclical supply-and-demand problem, factories could not make enough chips fast enough. The export controls from October 2022 onward are a structural, geopolitical restriction on where certain chips are allowed to go, regardless of how much factories can produce. The shortage has largely eased since; the structural restriction has not.

children.text: Modern cars run on dozens of chips, controlling everything from engine management to infotainment and driver-assistance features. During the 2021-2022 shortage, Indian automakers including Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, and Mahindra all reported production cuts and extended vehicle waiting periods, with industry estimates pointing to a meaningful chunk of planned production lost across the sector at the shortage's peak. The subsequent export control regime did not directly restrict India's chip access, but it added a new layer of supply chain uncertainty on top of an industry that had just been reminded how exposed it was to a global chip supply it does not control at all.
How This Hit, and Helped, Indian IT and Design

Indian IT services companies do not manufacture chips, but the effect on them cuts both ways. On the headwind side, a broader slowdown or increased uncertainty in global technology capital spending, partly a byproduct of this rivalry, feeds into demand for IT services from hardware and semiconductor clients. On the tailwind side, India is not just a bystander in the chip industry, it is a major back office for chip design itself. Global semiconductor companies including Qualcomm, Intel, AMD, and Texas Instruments run large engineering and design centres in India, and India is widely estimated to employ a significant share of the world's chip design engineering workforce, even while having very little chip fabrication capacity of its own. That design talent pool is arguably less exposed to export control risk than fabrication capacity would be, since the intellectual work product, not a physical chip, is what actually crosses borders.

body.label: India's Share of Global Chip Design Talent
body.value: Widely estimated near a fifth of the world total
body.context: A genuine structural strength, built over decades of global semiconductor companies setting up India engineering centres, distinct from and well ahead of India's still-nascent chip fabrication capacity

body.caption: The Four Channels, As Seen in This Case Study

cells: The dominant channel by far. Export controls are, by definition, a trade and supply chain restriction, and their effects on auto production and IT hardware clients flow through exactly this channel
A secondary effect, largely through investor sentiment toward Indian IT and auto stocks reacting to global tech spending trends, rather than a direct, mechanical link
Minimal direct relevance here, unlike the Russia-Ukraine case study earlier in this course
Minimal direct relevance here as well, this was not primarily a currency or risk-off event

body.text: Compare this to the Russia-Ukraine case study from Chapter 1, where energy and currency dominated and trade mattered comparatively little. Here, trade and supply chains dominate almost entirely, and energy and currency barely register. The same four-channel framework applies every time, but which channel actually carries the shock depends entirely on the nature of the event itself.

body.title: Two Sectors, Two Different Exposures
body.scenario: A new round of chip export restrictions is announced, broader than any before it. You hold shares in an Indian auto component manufacturer and an Indian IT services company with a large chip design engineering practice.
body.prompt: Would you expect both holdings to be affected the same way? Explain the likely difference in exposure.
body.modelAnswer: No, the exposures are meaningfully different. The auto component manufacturer sits closer to the physical supply chain for chips used in vehicles, so tighter restrictions could add sourcing uncertainty or cost pressure, similar to the shortage-era disruptions. The IT services company's chip design practice sells engineering expertise, not physical chips, so it is less directly exposed to export restrictions on physical goods, though it could still see indirect effects if global semiconductor clients slow their own capital spending amid the uncertainty.

body.title: Shortage vs Export Controls
body.question: What is the key difference between the 2021 global chip shortage and the export controls that began in October 2022?
options: They are two names for exactly the same event
The shortage was a cyclical supply-and-demand problem; the export controls are a structural, geopolitical restriction on where chips can go
The shortage only affected China, while export controls only affected India
body.explanation: The 2021 shortage stemmed from a temporary mismatch between chip supply and demand. The export controls from October 2022 onward are a deliberate, ongoing geopolitical restriction, independent of how much manufacturing capacity exists globally.

points: The 2021 global chip shortage, a cyclical supply-demand problem, and the export controls beginning October 2022, a structural geopolitical restriction, are related but distinct events that both hit Indian markets

Indian auto manufacturers faced real production cuts and extended waiting periods during the shortage, and the subsequent export control regime layered additional supply chain uncertainty on top of that exposure

Indian IT services carry mixed exposure: a headwind from global tech capital spending sensitivity, alongside a genuine tailwind from India's outsized share of the world's chip design engineering workforce, a strength largely insulated from export controls since it exports expertise, not physical chips
India's own semiconductor assembly and testing investments, including Micron's Sanand plant and Tata Electronics' facility, are a direct long-term response to this exact dependency

Applying the four-channel framework here shows trade and supply chains dominating almost entirely, a useful contrast with the Russia-Ukraine case study, where energy and currency dominated instead. The framework stays the same, but which channel carries the shock changes with the event
